pipeline.role: Deterministically map the 1449 historical tool-answer slots to replacement classes before text generation.
pipeline.reproducibility: Uses a fixed random seed and sorts the completed plan back by source index.
pipeline.critical_rule: The old answer is not reused as target prose; it contributes only source situation/domain/tool-output structure where relevant.

pipeline.role: Generate only free-text behavior while exact structural components are built by templates/orchestration.
pipeline.reproducibility: Output is append/resume oriented; interruption loses at most an in-flight batch rather than requiring a full restart.
pipeline.critical_rule: The orchestrator does not itself invent final training prose; free-text generation is delegated and then gated.

pipeline.role: Machine rejection gate before any human/blind review.
Merge accepted replacement examples into the training corpus while preserving original system texts 1:1 except the structured result block required by class 7.
pipeline.reproducibility: Builds an explicit blind sample with deterministic seed and emits measured reports.
pipeline.critical_rule: System-prompt rewriting is intentionally not smuggled into the answer-replacement stage.

reconciled_findings.finding: Plan, generation, rejection and assembly are separate executable stages. This is stronger than a single generation script because each boundary can be hashed, replayed and audited independently.

The historical design intentionally avoids repairing tool-calling answers in place. Replacement targets are generated from situation/structure rather than copying the old assistant prose, reducing direct imitation of the behavior being removed.

Structured facts such as result blocks, prior goals and placement metadata are generated deterministically; free models supply only language/behavioral prose. This is a direct historical precursor to current ClayCode/UnifiedDB typed-state plus language-projection architecture.

The blind-review artifact demonstrates that deterministic sampling is insufficient if the underlying source file is still mutating. Reproducibility requires both deterministic selection and an immutable generation-complete source hash.

Pattern-clone and near-duplicate rejection must run before manual quality scoring. High class quotas without lexical/structural diversity can produce a dataset that is numerically balanced but behaviorally narrow.

harness: Represent dataset construction as a four-stage DAG: plan -> generate -> reject -> assemble, with immutable manifests and hashes at every edge.
Require generation-complete barriers before blind sampling and evaluation.
Keep near-duplicate and exemplar-clone detection as pre-human gates.
unifieddb: Store source slot identity, class assignment, generator provenance, rejection reasons and final accepted artifact as distinct records rather than flattening them into one JSONL lineage.
claygraph: Expose provenance edges from original situation -> deterministic class plan -> generated candidate -> rejection/acceptance -> assembled training row.
claycode: Typed structural fields should be generated by deterministic code; language generation should consume those fields rather than regenerate them from prose.
frank: Behavioral training targets should not teach executable tool syntax when execution belongs to Needle; teach result consumption and state transitions instead.
needle: Preserve tool/effect ownership outside Frank's language target while delivering typed result/effect receipts back to Frank.
gwt: Goal/revision/abandonment/result states should enter workspace as typed events with provenance rather than as reconstructed narrative history.
